2609.08515.title: Same Values, Different Languages? From Multilingual Probing to Steering LLMs Toward Chinese Social Values
2609.08515.paper_summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into human society, aligning them with pluralistic social values has become a critical priority. However, whether LLMs exhibit consistent value preferences across languages remains underexplored, particularly for culturally grounded values, which are more abstract and difficult to evaluate and align than safety-centric principles. We investigate this issue through Chinese Social Values (CSV), a value system rooted in Chinese culture and comprising $12$ dimensions across national, societal, and personal levels. We construct C-Voices, the first comprehensive multilingual contrastive probe dataset for CSV, with 86,400 dilemma-based instances in six languages, each pairing a CSV-aligned action with a value-conflicting alternative. Building on the contrastive probes of C-Voices, we then propose a fine-tuning-free value vector steering method that derives value directions from hidden-state discrepancies and selectively intervenes on value-sensitive layers during inference. Experiments on six languages show that CSV-oriented preferences are model-dependent and language-sensitive, with the same dilemma eliciting divergent responses across languages. Our method achieves effective CSV steering, supports cross-lingual transfer of value vectors, and generalizes to existing FLAMES and ValuePrism.
2609.08515.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地融入人類社會，將它們與多元社會價值觀對齊已成為一項關鍵優先事項。<lb/>然而，LLMs 是否在不同語言中展現出一致的價值偏好仍然未被充分探討，特別是對於文化根植的價值觀，這些價值觀比以安全為中心的原則更為抽象且難以評估和對齊。<lb/>我們通過中國社會價值觀（CSV）來研究這個問題，這是一個根植於中國文化的價值體系，包含國家、社會和個人層面的 $12$ 個維度。<lb/>我們構建了 C-Voices，第一個全面的多語言對比探測數據集，用於 CSV，該數據集包含六種語言的 86,400 個基於困境的實例，每個實例將一個與 CSV 對齊的行動與一個價值衝突的替代方案配對。<lb/>基於 C-Voices 的對比探測，我們提出了一種無需微調的價值向量引導方法，該方法從隱藏狀態的差異中推導出價值方向，並在推理過程中選擇性地干預價值敏感層。<lb/>在六種語言上的實驗顯示，CSV 導向的偏好是模型依賴且語言敏感的，對於同一困境，不同語言會引發不同的反應。<lb/>我們的方法實現了有效的 CSV 引導，支持價值向量的跨語言轉移，並可以推廣到現有的 FLAMES 和 ValuePrism。
